Added CKMetrics.as_dict()/narrate(); new rules/class_shape.py; registered; test_rule_class_shape.py. summary.why: CK metrics are descriptive class-shape measures, not defects — NOC especially (a broad base is often a healthy abstraction), and DIT/NOC are inputs to the future taxonomic-degradation battery. Three standalone threshold verdicts would be false precision plus premature (subsumed by the battery). An observation makes no precision claim, so it cannot be a false positive — the emit-evidence-not-verdict path.

decisions.point: CK as three threshold verdicts, one verdict + deferrals, or an observation?
decisions.chose: A single class-shape observation per notable class; legacy thresholds become attention-floors.
decisions.rationale: NOC is ambiguous (healthy abstraction vs god-base); DIT/NOC are taxonomic-battery inputs not yet built; CBO's remedy is disjunctive. None is honestly a standalone scalar verdict. The observation surfaces the evidence and lets the agent judge, mirrors the vocabulary observation, and exercises the Class altitude + class_index path. Floors gate output volume, not pass/fail.
rejected: Three CBO/DIT/NOC verdicts (faithful legacy port): dishonest thresholds (esp. NOC) and battery overlap.
CBO verdict + DIT/NOC deferred: viable, but bundling all three as one class-shape observation is cleaner and avoids minting a coupling threshold whose remedy is disjunctive.

decisions.point: Where do as_dict()/narrate() live for CKMetrics?
decisions.rationale: The vocabulary observation is the blessed precedent: the measurement record owns its serialization + narration; the rule applies the floor and wraps in Observation. narrate() names only metrics past their floor and frames NOC as ambiguous (claim-free).
rejected: Narration logic in the rule: bloats the rule and diverges from the TokenDistribution precedent.
